name: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap geocoding)
description: Free forward and reverse geocoding over the whole OpenStreetMap database: address to coordinates, coordinates to address, with bounding boxes and administrative hierarchy. The public instance is donated infrastructure with a hard one-request-per-second rule, which is the only real catch.

license.name: ODbL 1.0
license.redistribution: share-alike; derived geodata must carry the same licence and attribute OpenStreetMap contributors

access.auth_note: no key, but a real User-Agent identifying your application is required by the usage policy and enforced
access.rate_limit: 1 request per second absolute maximum on the public instance, and no bulk geocoding at all
access.etiquette: cache every result; for more than a few thousand lookups, run your own instance or use a bulk geocoder

recipes.title: Geocode politely
recipes.code:
import json, time, urllib.parse, urllib.request
UA = 'my-project/1.0 (you@example.com)'   # required, and they check
def geocode(q):
    url = 'https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search?' + urllib.parse.urlencode(
        {'q': q, 'format': 'json', 'limit': 1})
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': UA})
    hits = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
    time.sleep(1.1)                      # the policy, not a suggestion
    return (float(hits[0]['lat']), float(hits[0]['lon'])) if hits else None

gotchas.trap: A default urllib or requests User-Agent gets blocked outright - the response is a 403 HTML page, not JSON.
gotchas.fix: Set a descriptive User-Agent with a contact address on every call.

gotchas.trap: ODbL is share-alike. Geocoding a private address list and publishing the result can pull your data into the same licence.
gotchas.fix: Read the licence before publishing anything derived from it; for many commercial uses a different geocoder is the safer choice.
